say: Because the friction pulls the cart back with 4 newtons, only part of your 10 newtons is left over to speed it up. You subtract the 4 from the 10 to get the net force, which is 6. Adding the two forces, 14, would mean friction is pushing the same way as the pull, which it isn't.
raw:
<say>Because the friction pulls the cart back with 4 newtons, only part of your 10 newtons is left over to speed it up. You subtract the 4 from the 10 to get the net force, which is 6. Adding the two forces, 14, would mean friction is pushing the same way as the pull, which it isn't.</say>
<visual>Lesson. Main idea: net force is the vector sum of forces, so opposing forces subtract. Cover: the pull of 10 newtons points right; friction of 4 newtons points left; the cart feels both; net force is 10 minus 4, which is 6 newtons to the right; then F equals ma gives a equal to 3 meters per second squared.
